title: observability-token-level-metrics-tracing-alert-tuning-enhancements
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: improve token-level observability for cost/latency breakdowns, tighten alert thresholds to reduce false positives, and add missing traces for KV cache hot paths. This PR introduces enhanced token-level metrics (token_emit_latency_ms, token_compute_cost_units, token_cache_hit), adds distributed tracing spans for KV cache hits/misses and batching boundaries, updates dashboards with new panels and breakdowns, and tunes alert rules to use rate/percentile-based thresholds instead of static counts. Changes include schema migration for metrics names, lightweight roll-forward compatibility, and a set of unit/integration tests for trace propagation. Checklist: - [x] Add token-level metrics and tags - [x] Add tracing spans for KV cache + batcher - [x] Add Grafana dashboard panels (cost/latency breakdown) - [x] Update alert rules and add runbook links - [x] Add end-to-end tests and mock metrics harness - [x] Docs for dashboard and alert explanations Links: Linear ENG-4023 (token-level observability rollout), ENG-4150 (alert tuning follow-ups), incident SUP-2214 for noisy alerts. Backwards compatibility: metric names are prefixed with redwood.token.* and we provide a shim to emit old names for 30 days. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag; dashboards updated in observability team workspace then promoted. Impact: expected reduction in paging noise and quicker debugging for tail-latency incidents. Breaking changes: none (shim included).

review_comments: Alex Chang: Nice work. Two questions: 1) does the metric cardinality increase significantly when we tag by route+model? 2) can we make the shim expiration configurable?

Priya Menon: Reply: cardinality analysis included in the PR description; we only tag with route/model for enterprise customers behind flag to limit cardinality. Shim TTL made configurable via config/observability.toml (defaults to 30d).
Marco Rivera: I saw a flake in the integration test on first run (trace propagation). Can you add a retry and ensure context propagation across goroutines?
Priya Menon: Added retries and explicit context propagation in batcher loop; re-ran tests locally and CI.
Lydia Park: Alerts look reasonable but suggest changing the 95th percentile window from 5m to 10m for lower-volume routes to avoid flapping.
Priya Menon: Updated alert rules: route-profiled rules use 10m window for low-volume buckets and 5m for high-volume buckets; added rationale to runbook.
